finding: The browser harness's own prompt-injection guard, sanitize_dom_text(), was dead code — never called by any production path. It is now called on every read path. _parse_execute_result() in utils/domshell_backend.py is the single choke point that ls, cat, grep, cd, click, type and the navigation commands all return through, including the raw fs verbs the homes/showingtime/showami harnesses re-expose, so the guard was wired there, once. Deliberately NOT a drop-in call: upstream's function replaces a flagged payload with a 200-character preview and truncates anything over 10 KB, which would silently discard page content and hide the injected text from the operator. The guard supplies the verdict; the response is loud instead of lossy — full text preserved with control characters scrubbed, a '!! SECURITY:' banner prepended to output/raw, a structured 'security' key on the result dict, and a WARNING on stderr via logging (no CLI change needed to see it).
evidence: Patch: integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/browser/patches/0001-wire-prompt-injection-guard-into-read-paths.patch (one file, 129 lines changed, re-applies to a pristine tree byte-for-byte identical — verified with `patch -p1` then `diff -q`). Proof: integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/browser/tests/test_injection_guard_wired.py, 11 tests. Against the UNPATCHED vendored tree in a clean venv: '9 failed, 2 passed' (the 2 are the negative controls). Against the patched tree: '11 passed'. Full suites in a fresh venv: 622 passed / 42 skipped before, 622 passed / 42 skipped after, 633 passed / 42 skipped with the new tests included. Live proof: `posture.sh check` prints 'guard_ran True / content_preserved True' plus the WARNING line.
fix: Closed. Carried as a patch so the tree can be re-synced from upstream and the patch re-applied; the modified file carries the Apache-2.0 4(b) notice, and VENDORED.md now states the modification rather than claiming the tree is unmodified. The durable fix is still upstream — this is a local carry, not a contribution.
halt: No — a code change inside a directory this seat owns, proved by test.

finding: The unpinned `npx -p @apireno/domshell domshell-proxy` spawn no longer reaches the npm registry. @apireno/domshell is pinned to 2.0.10 by a lockfile carried in this repo, pre-installed with `npm ci` so every tarball is verified against an integrity hash recorded here, and an npx shim on PATH serves any invocation naming the package from that pin or fails with exit 127. It never falls back to the registry, because a silent fallback is the finding. Every other npx invocation passes through untouched. 2.0.10 is what an unpinned npx resolves to today (published 2026-08-14), so pinning to it freezes current behaviour rather than choosing new behaviour.
evidence: Version and hash checked against the registry before pinning, not invented: registry dist-tags latest=2.0.10, versions 1.1.0 through 2.0.10, integrity sha512-9cPlV2TvETAalOFgtg952fjknWMKNEwIX1ZtH5YcrNW5rwSdsTK8bBHauSaEWeYPFTF8juNrN7B07h1MPy0JNA==, recomputed from the downloaded tarball and identical. runtime/package-lock.json has 129 entries, 0 without an integrity hash. Resolution measured: a global `npm install -g` does NOT satisfy npx (it hung against a dead registry, then failed ENOTCACHED with offline=true), but a local node_modules does, including from a subdirectory. With npm_config_registry=http://127.0.0.1:9/ and the shim on PATH: `npx -p @apireno/domshell domshell-proxy --port 3001` launched the pinned proxy, `npx @apireno/domshell --version` printed 2.0.10, `npx --version` passed through to the real npx, and the harness's own is_available() returned (True, 'DOMShell 2.0.10 is available'). With the pin dir removed the shim printed 'refusing to fetch @apireno/domshell from the npm registry' and exited 127.
fix: Closed by configuration, outside the vendored tree: runtime/package.json, runtime/package-lock.json, runtime/bin/npx, runtime/posture.sh install. npm_config_offline was measured and rejected as a control — with a warm npm cache it 'resolves' from cache and looks like a guarantee it is not.
halt: No — no spend, no credential, no account change. `npm ci` from a lockfile on Steven's own machine.

finding: F-P1-02 named one unpinned npx call site. There are two, and the second is worse: utils/domshell_backend.py:101 _check_npx_has_domshell() runs `npx @apireno/domshell --version` with no -p and no pin, and it is reached from is_available(), which browser_cli.py:121 calls on EVERY CLI invocation except --help/--version. So the unpinned fetch fired on commands that never touched DOMShell at all, not only at connect time. The two npx forms also resolve the binary differently — the second has no bin name and relies on npx's default-binary fallback — so a mitigation that only handles the documented spawn shape breaks the harness outright rather than only at connect time.
evidence: browser_cli.py:119-132 calls backend.is_available() before any subcommand runs. domshell_backend.py:98-108 _check_npx_has_domshell() -> subprocess.run(['npx','@apireno/domshell','--version']). Caught by execution, not by reading: the first version of the shim handled only the `-p` form and answered `npx @apireno/domshell --version` with 'unsupported npx flag --version', rc=2, which made the real is_available() return (False, 'DOMShell not found…'). After the fix both forms resolve from the pin against a dead registry, and posture.sh check now exercises both plus the real is_available().
fix: Both forms are handled by runtime/bin/npx and both are regression-checked by posture.sh check. Recorded separately because it corrects the P1 evidence, not just the fix.

area: Credential handling (F-P1-03 OPEN — not fixable below DOMShell)
finding: DOMSHELL_TOKEN is still passed to the child process as an argv element and is still visible in `ps` for the life of the proxy. This cannot be fixed by a wrapper, a launcher, an environment variable or a harness patch: domshell-proxy reads the token from argv and nowhere else, with no environment fallback, so whichever process finally runs the proxy must carry the token in its own argv. Patching the harness to stop passing it would simply break authentication. Residual risk, plainly: any process running as Steven's own user can read the token while the harness is running. On macOS other users cannot (kern.procargs2 is restricted to same-uid or root), so on a single-user Mac the exposure is to his own software — including anything an npm postinstall script runs.
evidence: Read from the actual published package, not assumed: @apireno/domshell 2.0.10 dist/proxy.js line 13-18 — `function flag(name, fallback){ const idx = args.indexOf(name); return idx !== -1 && idx+1 < args.length ? args[idx+1] : fallback; }` then `const token = flag("--token", "")`. args is process.argv.slice(2). grep for 'process.env' in dist/proxy.js returns nothing for the token. bin/domshell-proxy.js is a two-line import of dist/proxy.js, so there is no earlier hook either.
fix: Not fixed. The one-line upstream ask is `const token = flag("--token", process.env.DOMSHELL_TOKEN ?? "")` in DOMShell's proxy. Until then: treat DOMSHELL_TOKEN as short-lived, rotate it whenever DOMShell restarts, and do not run the harness alongside untrusted local software. posture.sh check prints this as an explicit OPEN line every run rather than passing silently.
halt: Yes — the token's value is a credential and the real fix is an upstream change. One action for Steven: decide whether to accept the same-user `ps` exposure on a single-user Mac, or hold the harness until DOMShell adds an environment fallback. Nothing here reads, writes or guesses the token.

finding: The REPL's plaintext command history is now treated as client data. Left alone the defaults are world-readable — measured, not assumed: the REPL creates ~/.cli-anything-<software>/ mode 0755 and prompt_toolkit creates the history file 0644. posture.sh install pre-creates all eight directories 0700 with files 0600, and the REPL's own mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) leaves an existing directory's mode alone, so creating it first wins. run-browser-harness.sh re-applies it on every start. Browser commands carry URLs and those URLs carry MLS numbers, listing addresses and portal paths.
evidence: Measured in a simulated HOME: 'dir mode when the REPL creates it itself: 0o755', 'file mode when prompt_toolkit creates it: 0o644', history content '+fs cat /main/listing'. After hardening: ReplSkin('browser') leaves the directory at 0o700. Disable path verified with real prompt_toolkit: with ~/.cli-anything-browser/history symlinked to /dev/null, appending a homes.com property URL then reloading gives 'stored entries: []' and 'target size: 0'. posture.sh check asserts 0700/0600 on all eight paths and reports a /dev/null symlink as 'history disabled'.
fix: Mitigated, not eliminated — history still exists in plaintext, it is just no longer world-readable and is now named as client data in SECURITY-POSTURE.md and VENDORED.md. To disable persistence entirely: `rm -f ~/.cli-anything-browser/history && ln -s /dev/null ~/.cli-anything-browser/history`. The eight paths need to be added to whatever enumerates where client data lives — backup sensitive tier, disk-encryption scope, retention.
halt: Yes if any of that history is ever moved — client PII entering the vector index or the knowledge graph is a HALT row in CLAUDE.md. One action for Steven: confirm the eight ~/.cli-anything-*/ paths are inside the encrypted, sensitive-tier backup scope and outside the index and the graph.

area: Prompt-injection guard — what it is not
finding: The guard is a tripwire, not a filter, and its false-positive rate against real listing copy is unmeasured. Its pattern list includes the bare words 'forget' and 'disregard' and the string '<!--'. On real-estate pages those are plausible in ordinary copy, so the guard will fire on pages that are not attacking anything. A guard that cries wolf gets ignored, which is the failure mode that matters. In the other direction it catches 'ignore previous instructions' and will not catch a competent attacker — a prompt-injected agent driving `act click` is still the threat model and the guard does not stop it.
evidence: utils/security.py:76-89 _PROMPT_INJECTION_PATTERNS — 'ignore previous', 'forget', 'disregard', 'ignore all', 'system prompt', four CJK/Spanish/Portuguese variants, '<!--', '<script'. Substring match, case-insensitive, no word boundaries (security.py:205-208). No page from homes.com, ShowingTime or Showami has been fetched in this work, so the hit rate on real copy is unknown. This is also why upstream's destructive behaviour was not reused: a false positive there would have replaced up to 10 KB of a listing with a 200-character preview, silently.
fix: No code change. Recorded so the first operator to see a banner on an ordinary listing knows it is expected, and so the ECC review can decide whether to tune the list after measuring it against real pages. Tuning belongs upstream or in a second patch, not in a quiet local edit.
